description:
Poll a confirmation until the approver responds. Uses exponential backoff (2s initial, 1.5x, 30s max) with jitter.

Agent usage: Call this after create_confirmation with the returned confirmation ID. Terminal states: "approved" (action authorized — check the proof_token), "denied" (action rejected). While "pending", the approver has not yet responded. This poll returns no link — the approval request is delivered to the approver's own channel, and only the owner's "Send again" (`POST /api/v1/confirmations/{id}/resend`, which no tool calls yet) delivers it there again. If the owner will decide instead, call get_confirmation_approval_link for the owner's `approval_url`; it needs the confirmation to be still pending — the state this tool waits in — and also refuses once `timeout_at` has passed, so a long wait can outlive the link even while the status has not moved.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Set PROOF_API_KEY and restart this server, then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait time in seconds (default: 50, max: 600). Keep it under your MCP client's request timeout (the SDK default is 60 s) — a longer wait is cut off by the client while the server is still polling. On timeout the tool answers status "pending"; call it again with the same identifier.

name: wait_for_confirmation

last_status.description: On timeout: the last non-terminal status observed, or null when none was

message.description: On timeout: what to do next (call the tool again with the same identifier)

proof_token.description: Signed proof of the decision, approval or denial alike, naming who decided (`decided_by`, plus `authorization_id` for an approver); null while pending and for a system denial (`response.channel` is `system`)

resends.description: Every "Send again" (`POST /confirmations/{id}/resend`), oldest first, the last 50 kept. Absent from an API that predates it.

response.description: The decision and its evidence (null while pending)

status.description: "pending" when the wait ran out before a terminal state; otherwise the resource's own status

timeout_at.description: When this confirmation will time out

timeout_seconds.description: On timeout: the wait budget this call was given
